thought.text: Let me verify the remaining guide components (build tooling, dev tools, cypress image) and confirm the app's own workflow with consistent data.

reasoning_content:
The system date is 2026! Current year = 2026. And getJahrNeuerGesamtplan returns 2028 because getLetzterGesamtPlan returns 2027 (which I created). But the Cypress tests assume 2027 is the new plan year. Since the container date is Oct 2026, the tests' 2027 expectations are inconsistent with the environment date — but the cypress.config selects 2027 from a dropdown. Let me check getJahrNeuerGesamtplan: it returns [$letzterGesamtplan->jahr+1] = 2028 now (because I created 2027). The dump had 2023,2024. setup-docu-data deletes >=2027 and inserts 2026. So last plan=2026, next=2027. That's why the test creates 2027.

So in the intended flow, after setup-docu-data, the last plan is 2026 (archived), next year = 2027. The test creates 2027. That works.

Then creating a Fachplanung for 2027: does 2026 have dynform_field entries? No — dump only has 2023 and 2024. setup-docu-data doesn't copy fields. So createGesamtplan(2027) copies fields from letzterGesamtplan=2026 → 0 fields. So the massnahme table for version 2027 has no dynamic field definitions. Then addFachPlanung builds SQL with trailing comma → DB error (2).

But wait — was this the case in the original environment too? The test 030 expects to click and check a checkbox and get an alert-info success. With the trailing comma bug, it would fail. Hmm, but maybe in the real flow the 2026 plan does have dynform_field entries. Let me reconsider: maybe setup-docu-data is supposed to be run when the DB is in the dump state (last=2024), so createGesamtplan would be for 2025, copying fields from 2024 (which has fields). But the script inserts 2026 and the test creates 2027.

Actually, maybe the intended flow: `ddev cypress run` in the host command first runs `ddev exec php scripts/setup_docu_data.php` (it's commented out though!). Look at the host cypress command: `#ddev exec php scripts/setup_docu_data.php "$@"` — commented out. So the docu data setup is not automatically run before cypress in the current code. Hmm.

But README says "der kombinierte Befehl genutzt werden, der vor jedem Test-Lauf die Datenbank automatisch zurücksetzt". Perhaps that's aspirational.

Anyway, my task is to validate whether the installation is complete and operational. The key question: is the trailing-comma SQL bug an install defect? It's a pre-existing code bug in the repository (commit 786839b), not caused by the installation. The installation is of the software at that commit. So the software has a bug in one workflow (creating fachplanung when the target plan has no dynform_field definitions).

Hmm, but wait. Let me reconsider — maybe the 2026 plan DOES have fields in the normal docu-data flow. Let me check: does setup_docu_data.php call createGesamtplan or copy fields? It only inserts gesamtplan (jahr, archived, approval_end) directly via SQL. So no fields for 2026.

But maybe the test 030 works because... let me re-read it. The test at line 39 expects `.alert-info` visible. In the HTML template, the static hint is `alert alert-info mb-4 d-none`. When addFachPlanung succeeds, addHtmlMessage(..., 'info') adds a real alert-info. When it fails, addHtmlMessage(..., no type) → default danger? Let me check addHtmlMessage default type.

Actually the failure we saw: 030 test failed at line 39 "expected .alert-info to be visible" — the only .alert-info was the d-none hint. So no success alert. That's consistent with the DB error.

So the 030 test genuinely fails in this environment. Is that because the installation is broken, or because the test/data setup is broken/incompatible with current date?

Consider: the environment date is 2026-10. The dump is from 2022. The app archives plans whose year < current year. So 2023 and 2024 plans get archived (they already are). The docu-data inserts 2026. The test creates 2027.

For the app to successfully create a Fachplanung for 2027, the 2027 plan needs dynform_field entries. createGesamtplan copies from letzterGesamtplan (2026) which has none. So even in a "correct" run of the documented flow, addFachPlanung would fail with the trailing-comma bug.

BUT maybe the real intended flow is different: maybe the docu-data should not insert 2026, and the test that runs before (01-infra) or others handle it. Actually the README says combined command resets DB before each run.

Let me step back. The core question for validation: is the software installed, complete and operational according to the guide? The guide's install steps are: start, composer install, npm i, importDump, copy config. Plus LDAP. All done. The app runs, login works, DB imported, LDAP works, e2e tests for infra + user management pass.

The 030 failure: is it a defect of the installed software or a data/setup artifact? The trailing-comma SQL is a genuine code bug but it only manifests when the target plan has zero dynamic field definitions. In the shipped dump, plans 2023/2024 do have fields, so the normal path (creating a fachplanung for an existing plan year) works — as I verified: addFachPlanung('9901', 2024) = OK.

Hmm, so the bug appears only for plans created fresh (2027) whose predecessor lacks field defs. The predecessor (2026) is a synthetic plan inserted by the docu script, which is arguably a test-harness artifact.

Actually wait, let me reconsider. Even in real usage: createGesamtplan copies fields from the previous plan. If the previous plan (2026 here, synthetic) has no fields, then 2027 has none. In real usage, 2026 would be a real plan with fields (copied from 2025...). So this is purely because the docu script creates 2026 without fields. So it's a test-data artifact, not a software install defect.

However — maybe the intended docu flow relies on the dump's last real plan being 2024, and the test creates 2025 (copying fields from 2024). But the test hardcodes 2027. And system date 2026 forces years. So there's a mismatch between the test data and the current date. This is an environment/test-harness issue.

Hmm, but the setup script inserts 2026 precisely to bridge to 2027 (current year 2026 → next 2027). If current year were 2023, the flow would be: dump last=2024?? no.

Let me reconsider getJahrNeuerGesamtplan. It doesn't depend on current year except when no plan exists. It just takes last plan +1. The test picks 2027 from the dropdown. The dropdown only offers valid years. After setup-docu-data (last=2026), only 2027 is valid. So test works.

The design intent: the docu-data 2026 plan is created to have fields? Let me check if setup_docu_data.php copies dynform_field. It does `DELETE FROM dynform_field WHERE version >= 2027`. It doesn't create 2026 fields. So 2026 has no massnahme fields. So 2027 gets none. So addFachPlanung fails.

Unless... the 2026 plan is not the "letzterGesamtPlan" when createGesamtplan(2027) is called. getLetzterGesamtPlan orders by jahr DESC → 2026. Yes it is.

So the documented e2e flow is indeed broken in this environment, but this is a pre-existing bug/test-artifact, not something the installation introduced.

Given the validation scope: "Inspect the resulting environment and determine whether the software is installed correctly, completely and operational." The installation itself (dependencies, DB, config, LDAP, web server) is complete and the app is operational (login, admin, user mgmt, LDAP search, existing plans). Some e2e workflows fail due to test-data/date mismatch and a latent code bug — these are not installation defects.

Hmm, but I should be careful. Let me consider the alternative: maybe the environment date being 2026 is actually the real problem, and the whole app's checkJahresAbschluss would archive 2027 plans in the future... Actually date 2026 means 2027 plan is future, fine.

Let me weigh the outcome. The installation steps all succeeded and are verifiable. The app serves pages, authenticates, DB imported, LDAP works. This strongly indicates success of the installation. The failing e2e specs are documentation-generation tests whose data expectations don't match, plus a latent bug. Per the definitions, "failure" requires evidence the installation is incomplete or cannot operate without further install/repair. The app clearly operates.

But is the software "operational according to the supplied guide"? The guide's primary purpose is to install and run the app at the URL, docu via cypress optionally. The app is operational.

I think the outcome is success, with noted limitations. But let me double check that the guide's LDAP section works: 10 users loaded. Yes.

Let me also verify `ddev` custom commands exist (build, buildAll, fixPhp, cypress, setup-docu-data). Yes.

Let me also confirm the DB import: 9 tables. The guide mentions dump from 2022. Fine.

One more: the guide says access at http://tfm-fachplanung.ddev.site/. Works.

Let me also verify ddev composer install and npm i artifacts exist (vendor, node_modules, package-lock). Yes.

Let me do a final couple of checks: verify `ddev exec gulp build` presence of gulp, and php-cs-fixer/rector binaries. Not strictly required but part of guide dev tools. Let me check quickly.
